Relates to #39950
This is a bit of an adventure.
It started in https://github.com/neovim/neovim/commit/d0c7f870c29cdea5b13547f58b97983cfde9b345, which enabled other output formats for the docs.

The goal now is to generate a PDF version of the user manual, without errors during generation but without worrying too much about how the PDF looks for now.

I'm not quite there. There are 2 errors, for one thing. The code still has some things copied over from the HTML version that need to be integrated properly (or discarded).

I'm opening this now because it's starting to feel like a rabbit hole :) And it would be interesting to have an outside look.

Goals before I squash the commits and open for review:
- no errors during generation ~(there are currently 2)~
- clean code with nothing copied as-is from the HTML version without making sure it's needed
- all the text of the user manual is present in the PDF

Non-goals:
- Provide a one-liner that will generate the PDF
- Fix all visual issues.The PDF doesn't look particularly good, especially the diagrams and anything where the actual layout of the characters matters (same problems as in https://neovim.io/doc/user/usr_02/#usr_02.txt, for example). But those issues are best addressed individually.

comment_data.body: This won't be part of the final commit - you can ignore it.

The other option is to consider that this is the responsibility of the code that will assemble the PDF, and the the current script only concerns itself with converting individual `.txt` files into `.typ`.

+--- Generates .typ from one :help file `fname` and writes the result to `to_fname`.

+--- @param text string|nil Source :help file contents, or nil to read `fname`.

+  local stats = {
+    noise_lines = {},
+    parse_errors = {},
+    first_tags = {}, -- Track the first few tags in doc.
+  }
+  local lang_tree, buf = parse_buf(fname, text)
+  ---@type nvim.gen_help_html.heading[]
+  local headings = {} -- Headings (for ToC). 2-dimensional: h1 contains h2/h3.

I haven't been able to work around that yet.
Links to other parts of the user manual are indistinguishable from links to the reference manual. But I'd like the former to work as links and the latter to just be formatted text.
I don't want to generate the entire reference manual at this time.

One solution could be to tell `typst compile` that links without labels are okay and that they should just be shown as text, but it doesn't seem possible.
Another solution is to do a second pass over the big `.typ` file and remove broken links before compiling... Not great.
Another solution is to punt this problem to the next iteration and just show text for now...

Ah yes, good point.
Actually, I can't find a case in the user manual where it's an actual column heading... I've found some [elsewhere](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/6f0d4ccc43d7c8f5dd72d0d83e54e947d05117fa/runtime/doc/options.txt#L2582-L2595).

For the most part it's used as an alternate code block, which indeed makes no sense but seems to have been done on purpose. I've found at least one place where both are used together:
```
The `echo` command evaluates its argument and when it is a number always
prints the decimal form.  Example: >

	echo 0x7f 0o36
<	127 30 ~

A number is made negative with a minus sign.  This also works for hexadecimal,
octal and binary numbers: >

	echo -0x7f
<	-127 ~
```
https://github.com/vim/vim/blob/27cfd1cf476d355060cd46bf7655ea547461ee0e/runtime/doc/usr_41.txt#L172-L182

Which indeed looks good within Vim, and bad [elsewhere](https://neovim.io/doc/user/usr_41/). Kind of like people mistagging OSM data in order to make it look good on their own app. I don't have a solution for that use case right now. It should really be just one code block.

OK for now I'll try to get away with "column_heading -> bold + respects whitespace", and iterate later.

And apologies to `tree-sitter-vimdoc` that I accused unjustly! I didn't realize that the `column_heading` was just set based on a concealed trailing tilde.
